BFA.note: No authentication, e-signature or mobile ID service stated.
No link between the civil register and the ID system stated.

facts.fact: Africa24 TV reports that the Yerekun unique electronic identifier, enrolled nationally since 11 November 2026, is framed by a 2024 law.

systems.owner: Government of Burkina Faso, WURI programme

facts.fact: Africa24 TV says a pilot of the unique identifier registered more than 16,000 people before the national enrolment launched on 11 November 2026, in a country of about 23 million.
Africa24 TV says the Yerekun 12-digit unique identifier is enrolled from age 5 and is intended to apply from birth.

A WURI project communications officer quoted by Africa24 TV says Burkinabe data are managed by Burkinabe engineers and specialists and hosted in Burkina Faso, and the identifier is described as locally developed.

BFA.note: The identifier is described as a unifying base for separate files, with no named register keyed on it.

facts.fact: Africa24 TV reports that national biometric enrolment into the 12-digit Yerekun unique identifier began on 11 November 2026 with 2,400 agents, about 12,000 planned sites and 966 biometric kits, after a pilot registering more than 16,000 people.

BFA.note: No other system checking against the identifier is stated.
Does not say government staff or a state body built or run a named system; only engineers managing data.
The identifier is not described as a population register.
Fraud in social aid is named as an aim; no registry link stated.
